registry_info.name: carriage_bench
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `travel` family (7 registry names, 1 wrapper script, 1 body, 1 shared const). One body stood up six times so the six mountings can be read against each other instead of one specimen at a time.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `travel` word and its six values are PRELOADED from cube_bearing.gd at runtime and the six mounts are built by cube_bearing.build() itself; do not retype them here or in the script.

carriage_bench.name: Carriage Bench
carriage_bench.description: Six identical cubes on one deck, each caught in a different one of the `travel` family's six mountings — none, seat, spindle, rail, gimbal, armature — built by the family's own static builder and lettered from its own const. `permit` is how much of what each mount concedes is drawn: the bare hardware, a glyph at every bearing, or a tally with a fixed ceiling of six. `reading` is what the bench counts as motion: everything, rotation only, or translation only — and the three readings rank the six mounts completely differently. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one freedom table derived from cube_bearing's own literals, read three ways.
interactions: walk the rank and find the two stations whose tallies read the same
compare the seat against the armature — a bed with chocks and a clamp arm, both conceding nothing
at reading=place, notice that the spindle reads rigid with its own wear ring in the frame
at counted, read the hollow slots rather than the filled ones
carriage_bench.qfep_connection: Six ways of holding one thing, and no stable ranking between them: which mount is the most permissive depends on whether you are reading position or orientation, so the order is a property of the instrument and not of the hardware. The `counted` rung is the bench's own dark spot — the moment it stops showing a constraint and starts showing a number — and it is built so the shortfall of the number is drawn in the same mark as the number.
carriage_bench.relationships: Synthesised from the seven registry names that declare `travel`, which resolve to one wrapper script over one body plus one shared const. It replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside; it calls cube_bearing.build() so the hardware in the frame is the family's own, not a copy.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The deck is 3.325 m along the rank by 0.53 m deep, so a 7 x 1 clear strip with room to stand in front. The tally skirt and the name tabs are on the +Z face and the graduations are inlaid in the deck reading from +Z, so the bench reads correctly approached from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through it — correct, because there is no bench, there is a picture of one.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of cube_bearing.gd's five builders plus this bench's own geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D (the six Label3D name tabs are not and do not enter it). X is 6 stations at 0.540 pitch plus 2 x 0.310 of end cell and margin. Y runs from -0.272 (the skirt's bottom edge, so the deck top sits at 0 and the mounts stand on it) to +0.460, which is the `none` station's dashed vertical translation arrow at the top of its cell; the tallest hardware is the armature's lock knob at +0.396. Z runs from -0.2634 (the gimbal's rotation arc, which overhangs the deck's back edge at -0.235 by 28 mm) to +0.307 (the tally slots standing proud of the skirt). The union is taken across all nine variants, which is what the sweep frames on.

dna.axis_shape: `permit` NESTS — bare is contained in swept is contained in counted, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew — so it is a sequence and must be swept in order. `reading` is neither a chain nor a set but a LATTICE: `motion` is the union of the other two and dominates both, while `pose` and `place` are INCOMPARABLE (pose sees the spindle and not the rail, place sees the rail and not the spindle, neither contains the other). Both cases are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a nested axis only lowers the ceiling, dropping one of two incomparable values loses a case. The declaration order puts the lattice's top first so a trim to two keeps the top and one of the pair rather than beheading the axis.
dna.default:
permit=swept, reading=motion. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is
nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in
doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That
freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `swept` AND NOT `counted`. `counted` is the loudest rung — it is the largest measured pair in
the whole sweep, bare <-> counted at motion, 57.97% focus — and it is the wrong default, because it
hands a visitor a number before they have seen the constraint it came from. `swept` is the rung at
which the bench's claim is legible without reading a scale: three arcs and three dashed arrows at
the loose cube, nothing at all at the seat, one arc at the spindle standing over its own wear ring,
one stopped arrow at the rail, two arcs at the gimbal, nothing at the armature. Six different
pictures, no caption. `bare` was also considered and passed over: it is the state all 31 family
placements ship in and it is therefore the honest control, but a default that says nothing about
what any mount concedes is a picture of the problem rather than of the artifact.

WHY `motion` AND NOT `pose`. `motion` is the top of the lattice and the only reading that gets
every station right. `pose` and `place` are each a real instrument and each is wrong about two of
the six mounts, which is the finding — but a visitor who meets only the default should meet the
bench working, not the bench failing. The failure is one token away.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the seven `travel` declarations leave unbuilt: cube_bearing.gd's own docstring lays the six mountings out as a comparison, and not one member can stand two of them at once, because a body can be in exactly one mount at a time.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A BENCH RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

How a thing is held decides what motion it is permitted, and a still cannot photograph motion but
can photograph a mount. cube_bearing.gd already knows this — it is the whole reason the family's
axis is the hardware and not the rate. What it cannot do is put two mountings next to each other,
because a body can be in exactly one at a time. Seven registry names declare the word and every
one of them STANDS IN one mounting and forgoes the other five.

So the bench stands the same body six times, in six mounts, on one deck, and varies what is SAID
about them.

THE ONE-SCENE-MANY-NAMES CLAIM WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, and it is stronger than the brief said.
All five pickup_cube_* scenes are the same wrapper to the byte: same script (pickup_wrapper.gd),
same three exports at the same values (rotation_speed 0, bob_height 0, bob_speed 0), same Area3D at
the same transform, same BoxShape3D(0.52), same half-scale Visuals slot, same signal connection.
The only line that differs is which scene is dropped into the slot. rotating_cube.tscn and
transformation_cube.tscn are that same body again — cube_scene.tscn — plus a tween and a `Travel`
child carrying cube_bearing.gd. Seven names, one wrapper, one body, one const.

WHAT IT FOUND, all computed before anything was built.

(1) THE FAMILY'S GIMBAL CONCEDES TWO ROTATIONS, NOT THREE. cube_bearing.gd says "orientation
conceded entirely" (l.60) and "orientation given away entirely" (l.306). Its code builds TWO
trunnion rings and two pairs of pins: yoke to outer on X at +/-1.87h (l.331-334), outer to inner on
Z at +/-1.645h (l.325-328). There is no third ring and no yaw bearing. The docstring claims three
degrees of freedom and the hardware has two. The bench counts the hardware.

(2) HARDWARE TELLS YOU ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT FREEDOM. Mesh counts and material volumes were
computed from the same literals (units of h^3):

  mount      meshes   volume    degrees of freedom
  none            0    0.000    6
  seat           10    3.529    0
  spindle         9    2.868    1
  rail            9    0.888    1
  gimbal          9    1.689    2
  armature       11    1.364    0

Over all six, volume and freedom correlate at r = -0.6933 — which looks like a law until you notice
it is carried entirely by `none`, the value with no hardware at all. Over the FIVE MOUNTS THAT HAVE
HARDWARE it collapses to r = -0.3095. Their mesh counts span 9 to 11, a 22% spread, while their
freedoms span 0 to 2. So the amount of material does not tell you how much a mount concedes; at
best it tells you WHICH freedom, and not even reliably — the seat has the most material of any
mount (3.529) and the armature the most parts (11), and the two of them concede exactly the same
nothing.

(3) THE SEAT AND THE ARMATURE ARE THE FAMILY'S TRUE PAIR, and they are the two whose hardware looks
least alike. A pad with four chocks and a keeper bar, against a column with a knuckle, a cranked
arm, jaws closed on the +X face and the lock handle thrown. Instantaneous freedom 0 and 0. Every
reading agrees; every tally row is identical; every glyph set is empty. What separates them is not
how much motion is permitted but WHO CHOSE THE POSITION — the seat's body is where it rests, the
armature's is where a previous hand put it — and that is a distinction no degree-of-freedom count
can carry. It is the bench's own limit, drawn.

(4) THE RAIL IS THE ONLY BOUNDED FREEDOM IN THE FAMILY, and its two numbers disagree. The hard
stops sit at c.y +/- 1.6h (l.296-298) and the carriage is 0.46h tall (l.300), so the carriage centre
runs +/-1.29h. The bright stripe rubbed into the slot is 1.6h tall (l.294), i.e. the carriage has
used +/-0.8h of the +/-1.29h available. Wear inside stops is consistent rather than contradictory,
and the bench draws the STOPS, because the axis is what the mount PERMITS. It is the only glyph on
the bench with stop discs on it; everything else is unbounded and carries open arrowheads.

(5) THE FAMILY'S DECLARED ORDER ALTERNATES. Arcs fall on none, spindle and gimbal, at positions 0,
2 and 4 — so no two adjacent stations both draw them. That is luck rather than design, and it is
why a 5.400H pitch is enough when two arc-drawing neighbours would have needed 5.180H of clearance
for the glyphs alone.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED, AND SO IS THE HARDWARE.
carriage_bench.gd opens with
const TRAVEL_SRC := preload("res://commons/primitives/cubes/cube_bearing.gd")
and the six station names, their count and their order all come out of TRAVEL_SRC.TRAVELS at build
time. The mounts themselves are built by TRAVEL_SRC.build(station, value, Vector3.ZERO, H) — the
family's own static builder, called once per station — so the steel in every frame is the family's
geometry and not a copy of it that could drift. `none` returns null before creating a node, which is
exactly the shipped look and exactly what the first station should be.

_check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in both directions: a value the family declares
that this bench has no freedom entry for, and an entry this bench holds that the family has dropped.

_check_hardware() is the second gate and the one that matters more. The freedom table (which mount
concedes which axes, and the rail's +/-1.29h) is a READING of cube_bearing's literals, and a reading
can go stale silently while the preload keeps working. So the bench measures each built mount's own
AABB in the station's local space and compares all six faces against dna-derived constants
(seat -1.500..+1.500 x -1.240..+1.440 x -1.500..+1.500, spindle 1.740/1.370/1.880/1.740, rail
-2.070..-0.330 x -1.750..+1.750 x -0.450..+0.450, gimbal 2.250/1.860/1.815, armature
+0.605..+2.600 x -1.225..+2.060 x -0.600..+0.600, all in units of h). A face that has moved more
than 0.005 m push_errors by name. If cube_bearing's hardware changes and this table does not, the
bench would go on drawing arcs for bearings that are no longer there, and nothing else in the chain
would object.

THERE IS ONE VOCABULARY AND IT DOES NOT COLLIDE. All seven registry entries carry the byte-identical
list [none, seat, spindle, rail, gimbal, armature] in the code's own order, with no member hoisting
its own default to the front — so unlike the `slack` family there are not even three orders to
reconcile, there is one. The corpus's adjacent words were checked before a new one was coined:
`support` (none|stand|frame|pylon, eight tokens), `mounting` (kiosk|lectern|wall, two) and `armature`
(none|datum|scaffold|gantry, two) all name HOW A THING IS PRESENTED, which is a different question
from what its mounting concedes, and the corpus keeps them apart. `permit` and `reading` are both
unused across all 434 declared axis words. `witness` and `mark` were considered for the second axis
and refused: each already carries two different meanings in the corpus and a third would be drift.
declines: `travel` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS. Refused for the reason retention_corridor refused `retention` and slack_yard refused `slack`, and stated here so nobody reopens it: each of the seven members uses the word to stand in ONE mounting and forgo the other five, so an axis over it would have six values each of which demolishes five sixths of this exhibit. The evidence that the values are PARALLEL and not nested is in the code, not the prose: cube_bearing's five builders share no geometry at all — _seat's ten meshes, _spindle's nine, _rail's nine, _gimbal's nine and _armature's eleven are five disjoint sets, and not one builder calls another. Nor do their freedoms form a chain: rail's single translation and spindle's single rotation are incomparable, and seat and armature concede the identical empty set through completely different hardware. There is no top value for an all-at-once frame to collapse into. So the word is exhibited — six stations, all six values standing in all nine tiles, lettered from the family's own const — and the bench varies what is said about them. A side effect worth naming: because `travel` is not swept, build_dna_gallery's tail-trimming can never drop `armature`. The brief asked for six values swept whole; standing them whole is the only way to guarantee it.

A `stance` AXIS THAT POSES THE BODIES. Designed and cut. It would have shown each body at the far end of what its mount concedes — the spindle's cube turned 45 degrees, the rail's raised to its upper stop, the gimbal's tipped onto a corner — which is a configuration and not a rate, so it survives the one-still rule. It was cut on geometry: the rail's carriage arm is built by the FAMILY's builder at c.y, so a body raised 1.29h would float free of the arm that is supposed to be carrying it, and repairing that means editing cube_bearing, which is the one thing a synthesis must not do. A drawn glyph can say `this could move'; a moved body has to bring its mount with it.

A `telltale` AXIS ON WHERE A POINTER IS BOLTED (corner | crown | flank). Built in the replica, rasterised, rasterised at 32.94% mean focus, and cut anyway. The idea was sound — a pointer on the axis of rotation is blind to it, so `crown` reports the spindle as rigid — but the geometry was fatal in two ways that only showed up in the picture. A pin short enough to keep the bench under four metres put its orbit at 1.5h, which is coplanar AND co-radial with the gimbal's inner trunnion ring at 1.44-1.58h: the drawn locus landed exactly on the hardware and the gimbal's ring simply turned cyan. And a pin long enough to clear the rings (>= 1.05h beyond the surface) would physically pass through the cage it is bolted inside. The blindness finding survived the cut and is now carried by `reading`, which needs no pin at all.

A `centre` TELLTALE, and with it the whole family of body-surface witness points. On a cube of half-side h, the orbit of any face centre about a body axis is the inscribed circle of a mid-section — entirely inside the body, tangent at four points, 0% visible. Only the corner escapes, at 1.4142h. Measured rather than argued: `face` scored 10.41% against `corner`'s 33.90% purely because two of its three orbits were buried in the specimen.

A FRAME-RELATIVE GAUGE. The tally's ceiling is six because a rigid body has six degrees of freedom, and it is six in every tile of every variant. The rail's arrow is 2.58H long because the carriage runs 2.58H, and it would be that length in a frame containing a mount that ran ten times as far. There is exactly one bounded freedom in this family, which is precisely the situation in which a bench is most tempted to invent a scale to fill its gauge. sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

A PROXY FOR FREEDOM. The tally counts degrees of freedom read off the hardware and nothing else. The tempting proxy was mesh count or material volume — it is available, it is easy, and it correlates at r = -0.80 with freedom across the five mounted values, which looks like a result. It is not one: it is carried by two outliers and it reports the seat (10 meshes, 0 freedoms) and the gimbal (9 meshes, 2) as near-identical. It is in dna.note as a finding and it is not on the bench as a mark.

LEAVING THE UNCOUNTED FREEDOMS DARK AT `counted`. The first tally drew `seen` filled slots and left the rest of the row dark. That makes `place` state that a two-ring gimbal and a chocked pad are the same thing, in identical rows, with no trace of the difference. The slots between `seen` and `held` are now drawn HOLLOW, so a reading that undercounts carries its own shortfall in the same mark. This is law 6 applied to the bench's own instrument rather than to the thing it measures.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, DURATION OR DECAY. A mounting has obvious time-domain axes — a speed, a settling, a duty cycle — and the family already refused them for exactly this reason: three registry names spell static/rotating/transforming longhand and all three are RATES. info_board shipped five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics body anywhere in this file, and the three rate exports the pickup wrapper carries are set to zero in all five of its scenes anyway.

STANDING THE GRADUATIONS UP. The first version gave `pose` a plumb index bar at every station and `place` a datum wire down the length of the bench, both at z = +2.70H. Six white posts stood in front of six mounts. They are now inlaid FLAT in the deck — a graduated rule along the front edge for translation, a graduated protractor ring around each station for rotation — where they still tell the readings apart at every rung and cannot occlude anything. The sight line was checked by ray, not by eye: see dna.still_note.
dna.measured: SWEPT 2026-08-12 at --max=16, all nine frames. Closest pair 0.21%, subject 13.5% of frame, and the pair is `permit` bare against swept AT reading = place. IT IS CONDITIONAL, not thin, and the structure is in the code: count_rot = reading != 'place' and count_tra = reading != 'pose', so at `place` only TRANSLATION freedoms are marked — and five of the six mounts on this bench permit rotation, not translation. Only `rail` has a translation to draw. So at that one reading, `swept` and `bare` are almost the same picture because there is almost nothing for a swept envelope to sweep, which is the bench telling the truth about what these mounts are. Grouped by context rather than by minimum, which is the only honest way to read a crossed axis: `permit` separates 1.34-3.20% at reading = motion, 1.20-3.06% at pose, and 0.21-2.07% at place. `reading` is the thinner axis in every column — 0.64% at permit = bare up to 2.88% at counted, with motion against pose the weakest pair everywhere, because a mount that permits rotation looks much the same whether you are reading its motion or its pose. Left alone. Inflating the place column would mean drawing a swept volume for a freedom the mount does not have.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels,
because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic
crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background,
converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below
come from rasterising this exact geometry - cube_bearing's five builders transcribed literal for
literal, plus this bench's own layout - at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62,
pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.56) in Python with a z-buffer, and pushing the result through
that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `permit` swept <-> bare AT reading=place, PREDICTED AT 6.25% FOCUS / 0.31%
FRAME. That is the strong half of the claim and it rules out the other seventeen pairs; the next
thinnest is swept <-> counted at place, at 17.12%, a factor of 2.7 away.

THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL AND IS THE POINT OF THE AXIS. At reading=place only translations are drawn,
and only two of the six mounts have any: `none` gets three dashed arrows, `rail` gets one stopped
arrow. So `swept` adds FOUR glyphs to a six-station rank, against ten at reading=motion. The same
pair at motion measures 35.35% and at pose 31.70% - a 5.7x spread across the crossed axis, which is
the conditional-axis shape csg_union_demo taught the critic to look for. Do not read `permit`'s mean
as its verdict; group by value pair across contexts.

FULL PREDICTED TABLE, focus / frame, all eighteen same-axis pairs:

  permit                         reading      focus    frame
  swept <-> bare                 place        6.25%    0.31%
  swept <-> counted              place       17.12%    0.88%
  swept <-> counted              pose        20.02%    1.02%
  bare  <-> counted              place       23.16%    1.19%
  swept <-> counted              motion      24.05%    1.22%
  swept <-> bare                 pose        31.70%    1.58%
  swept <-> bare                 motion      35.35%    1.77%
  bare  <-> counted              pose        50.56%    2.61%
  bare  <-> counted              motion      57.97%    2.99%
  AXIS MEAN                                  29.58%    1.51%

  reading                        permit       focus    frame
  motion <-> place               bare        19.80%    0.99%
  motion <-> pose                bare        23.24%    1.16%
  motion <-> pose                swept       25.65%    1.28%
  motion <-> pose                counted     29.73%    1.49%
  pose   <-> place               bare        43.04%    2.15%
  motion <-> place               swept       46.43%    2.35%
  motion <-> place               counted     48.16%    2.70%
  pose   <-> place               swept       60.46%    3.63%
  pose   <-> place               counted     60.46%    3.92%
  AXIS MEAN                                  39.66%    2.19%

SO THE PREDICTED VERDICTS ARE `reading` BITES AND `permit` LOCAL, and that split is itself the
prediction. The critic calls an axis LOCAL when focus clears 12% but frame stays under 2%, and
`permit` lands at 1.51% frame against `reading`'s 2.19%. It is not a weakness and it should not be
read as one: a six-station rank is 3.325 m wide and its glyphs are centimetres, so a frame-wide mean
is the wrong statistic for it. If `permit` comes back BITES instead, the showcase key light is
putting more specular on the emissive glyphs than a flat-shaded replica models, and the number to
check is the frame mean rather than the focus.

THESE NUMBERS MOVED ONCE, BY 9%, FOR A REASON WORTH RECORDING. The first replica and the first
draft of the script both built every rod, arrowhead and stop disc on a basis whose determinant was
-1 - Basis(xv, d, d.cross(xv)) instead of Basis(xv, d, xv.cross(d)) - so every glyph was mirrored
and lit on its wrong face. A cylinder is rotationally symmetric, so this is invisible in the
silhouette and would only have shown up as glyphs mysteriously darker than the hardware around
them. It was caught by reading the handedness, not by the picture, and correcting it moved
`permit` from 32.31% to 29.58% and `reading` from 42.52% to 39.66%.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If the closest pair comes back as `reading` motion <-> place at bare (predicted 19.80%) instead,
    the replica overstated how much a flat inlaid graduation survives the 160 x 160 downsample. That
    pair is the whole difference between a rule strip and six protractor rings lying on the deck,
    both at 5.0 px of tube on a 269 px crop, and flat marks are the part of this bench most likely
    to be lost in the resize - 269 px of crop height at 0.5948 samples per pixel.
(b) `permit` swept <-> bare at place is predicted at 6.25%, which is a quarter of a point above the
    critic's 6% TWIN_FOCUS bar. If it lands under, it will be re-measured per channel and should
    read much higher: the four glyphs are green (0.42, 0.90, 0.55) on a neutral deck
    (0.205, 0.200, 0.196), and the critic is colour-blind in luminance by design. Expect it in the
    COLOUR-ONLY list, not in twins.
(c) If any pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=carriage_bench first, and
    then check that the script LOADS - passing the declaration gate is not evidence that it does,
    because that gate reads @export_enum hints out of the source text and never parses the file.
    slack_yard shipped four constructor-call constants that made its script unloadable while the
    gate reported both its axes ok.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. At `counted`
the tally rows for pose and place read 0 at four of the six stations each - seat and armature under
both, plus rail under pose and spindle plus gimbal under place - and both readings blank most of the
bench. They are not twins and should measure far apart (predicted 60.46%), because the two readings
blank DIFFERENT stations and each brings a different graduation with it. If that pair does come back
tight, the protractor rings and the rule strip are not surviving the downsample and finding (a)
above is the cause, not the axis.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL NINE FRAMES, not from the default. Union
3.325 x 0.732 x 0.5704 (x = along the rank, z = across the deck); diagonal
sqrt(11.0556 + 0.5358 + 0.3254) = 3.45207, radius 1.72603. The rig is
dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera
at 1.72603 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 10.7266 m and shows a 6.5589 m frame around a 3.325 m object — PAD
1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well
below 1.0.

AT 0.56 the camera comes to 6.0069 m and the frame to 3.6730 m, which is 206.9 px per metre. The
subject's projected width is 3.325 x 0.8138 + 0.5704 x 0.5811 = 3.0373 m, or 82.8% of frame, with
0.3178 m = 66 px of clear margin each side; its projected height is 1.3235 m, 36.0%. Rasterised at
that setting the subject covers 7.55% of the frame at `bare` and 10.02% at `counted` — above the ~6%
dilution floor and far above the blank-render check. 0.52 was measured too (89.5% of width, 42 px
of margin) and rejected: 42 px is not enough slack for the showcase key light's specular fringe,
which the replica does not model, and slack_yard's own margin test wanted 58.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: `counted` adds a 0.21 m band of tally slots to the skirt and
`bare` does not, so the subject box is 245 px tall at bare and 269 at counted. Framing off the
default would have moved the camera between rungs of a NESTED axis, which is the one place it must
not move. The deck is deliberately the full 3.325 x 0.53 at every value of both axes, so the box
does not change for any other reason.

GAUGE CHECK AT 206.9 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane.
Body 0.200 m -> 41.4 px; arc tube 0.028 -> 5.8 px; arrowhead 0.064 -> 13.2 px; stop disc 0.052 ->
10.8 px; protractor tube 0.024 -> 5.0 px; rule strip 0.028 -> 5.8 px; body edge bar 0.020 -> 4.1 px;
tally slot 0.072 x 0.105 -> 14.9 x 21.7 px; tally divider 0.020 -> 4.1 px.

AND THE SAME CHECK IN THE CRITIC'S OWN SAMPLE SPACE, which is the one that bit sorting_hall. The
crop here is 629 x 269 px and it is resized to 160 x 160, so a screen pixel is 0.2544 samples across
and 0.5948 down — an asymmetric squeeze of 3.93x in x against 1.68x in y. A tally slot is therefore
3.8 x 12.9 = 49 samples of ink; an arc tube is 1.5 samples across but 51 px = 12.9 samples long in
x and 32 in y, because it is a long curve and not a dot. Every glyph was widened from 0.09H to 0.14H
for this reason and no other: at 0.09H the arc tube measured 3.7 px and 0.95 samples, which is
sorting_hall's three-pixel gauge with one dimension to spare.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The
file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no
Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is
ungated: it reads config metadata, validates the family list and builds the whole bench standalone,
so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE FAMILY'S BUILDER IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION and says so in its own header: every
dimension in cube_bearing.gd is a literal multiple of the measured half-extent, with no RNG
anywhere. This bench passes it a constant half-extent (H = 0.10) and a constant centre
(Vector3.ZERO in the station's own space), so two captures of one value are two photographs of one
object.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps
config_permit / config_reading metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks the ancestor chain for
before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against
_is_permit / _is_reading, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND
_ready has already built once — the force_pad fault.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the
string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. Both @export_enum hints are on ONE line, so the
declaration gate's line parser can see them.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read
correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES, by construction: the deck, the skirt, the seven tally
dividers, the six mounts and the six bodies. Those are the control, and they are 100% of the frame
at bare/place. Everything that changes is measurement apparatus, which is what both axes are about.

THE Z-STACK, WRITTEN OUT, because operations_gallery's bezel was one 24 mm slab enclosing every mark
its axis drew and its numbers looked exactly like an honest axis diluted by furniture. Camera at
+X +Y +Z, deck top at y = 0:
  deck slab      y [-0.042, 0.000]   z [-0.235, +0.295]
  front skirt    y [-0.272, -0.042]  z [+0.275, +0.295]
  tally slots    y [-0.272, -0.062]  z [+0.295, +0.307]
  rule strip     y [ 0.000, +0.006]  z [+0.256, +0.284]
  protractors    y [ 0.000, +0.006]  radius 0.216..0.240 about each station
  mounts         y [+0.020, +0.396]  z [-0.182, +0.182]
  bodies         y [+0.090, +0.290]  z [-0.100, +0.100]
  arcs           y [+0.068, +0.449]  |z| <= 0.259
NOTHING OPAQUE STANDS BETWEEN THE CAMERA AND A MOUNT, and it was checked by ray rather than by eye.
The graduations lie FLAT at y = 0.006 and the skirt hangs BELOW the deck at y < -0.042, while every
mount starts at y = 0.020. A ray from the lowest mount pixel (y 0.020, z 0.180) toward the camera
has risen to y = 0.049 by the time it reaches the rule strip at z = 0.270 and to y = 0.059 at the
skirt at z = 0.300. The first version stood the graduations up and six white index posts stood in
front of six mounts; that is why they are inlaid.

THE TALLY DIVIDERS ARE NOT DECORATION. The skirt sits 0.27 m in front of the mounts and the camera
stands at yaw 0.62, so that offset projects to 0.27 x 0.5811 = 0.157 m of screen width — about a
third of a station pitch. Without a divider at each station boundary the tally row reads as
belonging to the station on its left. Measured in the replica before they were added.

TWO STATIONS THAT SHOULD MEASURE THE SAME, AND IT IS NOT A FAULT: `seat` and `armature` draw no
glyph under any reading and an all-dark tally row under all three. Their hardware looks nothing
alike and their freedom is identical. Do not "fix" it — it is finding (3) in dna.note and it is the
bench's own limit made visible.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are six Label3D in the artifact and they letter the six mounts —
none, seat, spindle, rail, gimbal, armature — which are present at every value of both axes.
Billboard is DISABLED on all six, which also keeps LabelFramer out: it treats billboard-enabled as
the hanging signal and would bolt a panel and a bezel behind each one, six slabs this bench did not
ask for. Label3D is not a MeshInstance3D and does not enter the capture AABB.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh, CylinderMesh,
TorusMesh, plus the family's own SphereMesh balls), there is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG and no
particle system, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 9? A 3x3 declaration is exactly the gallery's default cap, so nothing should
    trim — but at --max 6 `reading` would be measured on [motion, pose] alone and the verdict would
    be about two values published as a verdict about three.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 3.325 m bench is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would
    be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every glyph would shrink.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The rank runs along X, which projects at 0.8138 per metre
    against Z's 0.5811, and the arcs stand in three mutually perpendicular planes — the one about Y
    lies flat and foreshortens to 0.2092 per metre while the other two stand up at 0.9664. A probe
    from directly above would flatten the two vertical arcs and open the horizontal one, which is
    the opposite bias. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until
    tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
